utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution would like to address the Chamber in private session. We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The next witness who can be brought into the courtroom will testify with protective measures of pseudonym, face distortion, and voice distortion. I do understand that the voice distortion has been prepared.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls JF-018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JF-018. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Witness JF-018, because that's how we will address you, the Chamber has decided that you will give your testimony under pseudonym, that is, we'll not use your own name, we'll just call you Witness JF-018. Further, your face cannot be seen by the outside world, neither can your own voice be heard. The image of your face will be distorted. Your voice will be distorted. However, the content of your testimony is publicly available, but, again, without seeing your face, without hearing your own voice, and without using your own name. May I remind the parties that for voice distortion that it's necessary to switch off your microphones once the witness starts answering the questions. Witness JF-018, you'll first be examined by Ms. Friedman. Ms. Friedman is counsel for the Prosecution and is seated to your right and will soon stand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Can I ask the Court Usher to please call up 65 ter 5276, which is the witness's pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any technical problem? Because the pseudonym sheet which is not to be shown to the public does not appear yet on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it would assist, I could provide a hard copy to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's perhaps preferable in order not to lose any -- there we are. There we are, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Could the document be enlarged a little bit for the witness to see. Thank you. And I take it it is not being broadcast? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sir, would you take a look at the pseudonym sheet in front of you on the screen before you, and if you direct your attention to where it says witness name, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And where it says date of birth, is that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the pseudonym sheet would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P339, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P339 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall giving a statement to members of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in relation to this case?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would now ask that 65 ter number 5274 be placed on the monitor in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Not to be shown to the public. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the English is the original, although usually we have both versions on our screen. Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: They are now both on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen before you is a document purporting to be a statement given by you on the 21st of January, 2001. Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise any signatures on the bottom of the page in the English version?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would ask that the Court Usher turn to page 4 of the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And, sir, do you again recognise any signatures on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes, my own.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to review this statement this past weekend in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Is there any clarification you wish to make?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I have clarified a few things. I've made some changes to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. On page 3 of your statement in the first full paragraph you state: "As the building in Dalj was destroyed, we used the old Zadruga building." Was the police building in Dalj destroyed?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No, it wasn't destroyed. It was just damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And on the same page in the last paragraph, you state that: "... a group of armed men in camouflage uniforms arrived in a TAM 110 military truck." Do you have anything to clarify with respect to this sentence?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: They came in two trucks, or at least two trucks. There wasn't just one truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And having --

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Could have been even more.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Having made these clarifications, do you affirm that your statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today as you were asked during that interview, would you provide the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders into evidence 65 ter 5274, which is the statement of this witness dated 21 January 2001 bearing the English ERN 0200-0600 to be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? In the absence of any objections, Madam Registrar, could you please assign a number to the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P340 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P340 is admitted into evidence. I put on the record that when you asked the witness to look at page 4 for his signature, that as a matter of fact page 5 which also bears his signature was shown to the witness. Both in hard copy and in e-court page numbering it was page 5. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now that the witness's prior evidence has been tendered pursuant to Rule 92 ter, I would like to read a summary of that evidence for the benefit of the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. You have explained the witness what the purpose is, otherwise I will do it briefly. Ms. Friedman will now summarise what is in your statement because although no one can see your face, although no one can hear your voice, and your identity is protected, nevertheless, the public is entitled to know what the content is of your statement about which further questions may be put to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. JF-018 has provided evidence that one day in early October 1991 he found out that a group of some 30 men were detained in one of the rooms of the Zadruga building where the milicija was based. The witness provides evidence about how several days later a group of Arkan's men arrived armed at the Zadruga building and that he heard afterwards that they had taken the prisoners away and killed them. After this incident, Arkan was called to explain what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: JF-018, what I have read is only a summary, it does not serve as your actual evidence. However, I would like to ask if you anything that I have said is a mischaracterisation or a misstatement of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. It's recorded as saying yes that there is a misstatement or mischaracterisation. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No, what you have read is accurate. This is an accurate, brief description of what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman, seeking such verification where the summary is now evidence, where the evidence is available, usually leads to more confusion than to clarity, so therefore, I would encourage you to refrain from the same. But it may be that in other Chambers, matters are different. I never sought such a verification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I'll ask you some additional questions. On page 3 of your statement, the first paragraph which continues from the previous page, you talk about the 1st of August, 1991, and state: "In the afternoon, JNA trucks brought weapons and they were distributed among Serb villagers." How were these weapons distributed?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Everybody who was issued with a weapon had to sign a document indicating the type of rifle that they were issued with.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: What ethnicity were the police officers at the time?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: They were mostly Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: How many of these men were professional policemen before the war?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many. I knew of two of them, that they were policemen before the war, but there may have been others. I'm sure of those two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And how many shifts were there in each day?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Three shifts. The first one was from 6.00 in the morning until 2.00, the second one from 2.00 to 2000 hours, and the third shift was from 2200 hours to 6.00 in the morning again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, your answer is recorded as saying that the second shift was from 2.00 to 20 hours and the third was 22 to 6, which leaves a gap between 20 and 22. Could you repeat again the times of the last two shifts if there is a clarification to be made?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: As I already stated, the second shift was from 2.00 until 2200 hours and the third from 2200 to 6.00, and we did not work every day. We worked for two days then we were off, and then again we worked for the next two days. And that's what I already stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you about the setup of the Zadruga building that the milicija was using. How many entrances were there to this building?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Just one. And the building it surrounded with other buildings from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And if you enter the building in the direction of the offices, would you pass directly by the room where the prisoners were kept when there were prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, you could do it that way, but there was another room before that, an ante-room as it were. First there was this first room through which you had to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: You stated at page 3 of your statement in the last paragraph that Arkan's unit was based in Erdut. Did you ever pass by their base?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you observe them doing?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, sometimes you could see them training, jogging, serving as guards, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Other than the incident in October 1991, which we'll talk about shortly, are you aware of Arkan's men coming to Dalj at other times?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, they drove around. You could see them frequently driving around. Sometimes they would intercept people, some older people who wouldn't be in the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: What do you mean by them intercepting these people?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, older men did not go to the front line. They didn't take part in combat. They would just serve as guards in the village and so on. But Arkan's men would force them to go to the front line, they would stop them and then they would beat them up because they didn't go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Turning once again to the last paragraph of page 3 of your statement, you state that Arkan's men: "Were armed with automatic assault rifles." Can you provide any additional information about their weapons?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you. They had all kinds of weapons. Very sophisticated. I even saw some Hecklers, some very sophisticated weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: In your statement on page 3, last paragraph, you stated that one night in early October 1991, at around 2215, a group of armed men arrived at the police station. And you then clarified that they were Arkan's men. Now, what did they say when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: They demanded that the prisoners be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what did the police -- what did you respond?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, we wouldn't let them take these people away because they didn't have any papers on them, no documents, so we didn't want to let this happen. We wouldn't surrender these men to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, nothing. They left and then returned. They left. And then we went on patrol in our vehicle. We just went about our regular duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: On page 4 of your statement in the first full paragraph you state that: "I learned from the duty officer that some of the prisoners that had been detained in the milicija building were killed [Realtime transcript read in error "trained"] by Zeljko Raznatovic, aka Arkan's men, and their bodies were thrown into the Danube River at a place called Jama." Did you see any prisoners in the building when you returned?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: When we returned in the morning, we saw one of them. He was sweeping the ground in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Why was he sweeping the ground?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, because there was blood outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Do you know if he was part of the same group of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity he was?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: On page 4 of your statement in the first full paragraph, you state: "I believe that all of the milicija men from Dalj signed a petition that condemned the incident." Did you sign such a petition?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: On page 4 of your statement in the next paragraph you talk about a gathering of civilians, milicija men, and members of the TO units where Arkan arrived and held a speech. You state that you were on duty and did not hear what exactly he said. Did you subsequently hear from others what Arkan said?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: They said that he admitted at this gathering that he had killed those men.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Friedman. Sequence of cross-examination will be? Mr. Jordash will be the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-018, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. You may proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I have very few questions, Mr. Witness. Probably less than 10 minutes. I want to ask you, if I may, about the reaction of others to Arkan's removal of the prisoners. Am I correct that the signing of the petition by the militia men came about through a collective outrage at what Arkan and his men had done?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it wasn't just them, the policemen, who were outraged; it was the population overall, the people there, because of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when you say "the population overall," can you explain to the Court who you are referring to? Who shared that outrage?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, for the most part I'm talking about the people from Dalj because this happened in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the majority of the people in Dalj were Serbian at that time?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes, a majority. But there were also some Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if other Serbians in other villages around Dalj also were outraged or disapproved of Arkan's behaviour in removing the prisoners and executing them?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I don't know, but most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if there were TO members in Dalj at around that time?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did they, as far as what you saw or heard, share your outrage at what Arkan had done?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes, they did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear at that time that Arkan was collaborating closely with high-ranking members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You didn't hear that?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear that when he was summonsed -- sorry, let me start that again. Who summonsed him to come and explain himself, do you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, someone from the command of the TO staff and the police commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When he came to the meeting, do you know if he came accompanied by JNA officials?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No. I wasn't there when they arrived. We just saw their vehicle, his vehicle, a jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know why the TO or the militia didn't attempt to arrest Arkan at that time?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, no one could do anything about Arkan at the time. He had his own army. They called them the Serbian guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest that the TO and the militia and the civilians couldn't do anything because Arkan was closely collaborating with the JNA and they would, it was anticipated, prevent such an arrest?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I've got no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I invite the parties to look at page 16, line 18. Ms. Friedman, I don't know whether you read "trained" or not, and it is a mistake which will not be easily detected when the transcript is corrected, but page 4 of the statement reads that some of the prisoners that had been detained in the milicija building were "killed" by Zeljko Raznatovic, also known as Arkan's men. And this, I think, should be corrected in order to avoid confusion. Mr. Bakrac or Mr. Petrovic, who is going to cross-examine the witness? Witness JF-018, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Bakrac is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My learned colleague Mr. Jordash asked you about Arkan and his men, and you described the incident on the critical evening in question. My question is this: Were you at the police station building on the evening when Arkan came with his men to the police station?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No. Only when his men came on that first occasion. Not on the second occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, your question implied that Arkan came with his men on the critical evening. If you wanted to refer to the night of the 31st of July -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are reminded again that we should switch off our microphones when the witness answers the question. Now, let me have a look. Now, you may have looked at the B/C/S version as well, but I noticed that in the statement often reference is made to Zeljko Raznatovic, also known as Arkan's men; that is ambiguous because I understood it to be that Arkan's men, Arkan's real name being Zeljko Raznatovic, came. Now, in your question you take a different approach. You are talking about Arkan arriving with Arkan's men. I don't know whether you understand it in a different way because from the statement it appears to me that after the events, Arkan appeared and gave a statement in the absence of the witness on the -- on a central place in the village. I'm getting confused by your question, or did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, perhaps I wasn't precise enough. But what you are referring to is the second incident. In other words, after the prisoners had been taken away as far as I understood it, Arkan came and addressed those persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac, you were talking about that critical night, I mean, no wonder that we get confused. If you would be very precise in your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you don't know, in other words, the date of that critical evening, or night, when the prisoners were taken away, those prisoners who were later found dead? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date exactly, but it was in August. But I don't know exactly what day in August. I don't know if it was the 8th or 9th. I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, on that night, the date of which we don't know exactly, when those prisoners were taken away, did Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, come with his men or did some men come that you referred to as Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I didn't even know Zeljko Raznatovic until I saw him on TV later on. As for his men, they had insignia, they had a tiger patch, and it said Serbian guards, and that's how I could tell that it was them. But I didn't know him. I only saw him on TV later on. It was only his men who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When they came, what did they do? Did they actually go into the police building, police station building?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No. They stopped at the entrance. We did not allow them to come in. They wanted to come in, but we wouldn't allow them to come in because they didn't have any papers on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not allow them to come in without the proper paperwork. Now, in your statement, as far as -- or if I understand you correctly, you said that members of Arkan's volunteer guard used to come into the police building in Dalj; is that correct? Earlier on?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know, but I heard this from some other people who also were patrolling in shifts, but it didn't happen while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you did hear it from your men that earlier on they did come in, probably they were permitted to come in?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know, because you worked at the police at that time, who it was who issued permits or passes? You said that you didn't allow Arkan's men to come into the building without some papers or the pass or permit. Now, who was it who actually issued these passes?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: At the staff command, the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So when we say the TO command staff, we mean the Territorial Defence of Dalj that was subordinate to the Territorial Defence staff of Baranja; correct? You are referring to the local TO staff?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever heard of Kozara, the boat Kozara?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that the army command was actually headquartered on a boat that was moored some distance away from there?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the critical night when the prisoners were taken away, did you see Mr. Stricevic at the police station by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Stricevic was?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was he the commander of the local Special Police who dubbed themselves the space police?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did this police and Stricevic, were they also part of the Baranja Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, I just have one more question and then I will complete with this part before the break, Your Honours. But I'm not sure whether it should be asked in closed session. And out of an abundance of caution, I would appreciate if we could move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, there's just one last thing that I would like to ask you about, if you can answer it. And if you don't know anything about it, it's quite okay if you say I don't know. I would like to know what the relationship was between the TO and the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in your area in the relevant period about which you are testifying here, in other words, August/September 1991. I apologise, I mean the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I am sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what the relationship was between the TO, the local Territorial Defence, and the JNA that came at that time to defend the Serb people? And I'm referring to August and September 1991.

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: I believe that the TO was under the JNA command or it should have been at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And one more question, Mr. Witness, do you know who Mr. Mile Paspalj was?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. And really, my final question now, do you have any knowledge about the fact that in the course of 1992 or 1993 Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, was a minister without a portfolio in the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you. You told us - that was the last question put to you by Ms. Friedman - that you heard from others that Arkan would have admitted at the gathering that he had killed those men. Do you remember who it were that told you this? Did you know the persons who told you what Arkan had said?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: He said that himself in front of the hundreds of people who were there. I don't know who said it exactly but everybody was talking about that because everybody had heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were these people you knew? Were these colleagues, neighbours, this kind of -- what do I have to understand it? It was the talk of the town, is that what you intend to say?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And was the talk of the town about what had happened, or did everyone also talk about what Arkan had said about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Ms. Friedman, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Just one short matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sir, at page 23 of today's transcript, line 20, you were asked if you know who Stricevic was, and you said yes. I wanted to ask you if you were every introduced to Milorad Stricevic?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No. I knew him by sight. I used to see him around the village at the time. I may have exchanged a word or two with him, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Did you know him before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JF-018
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have the questions from the Bench or the questions of re-examination triggered any need for further questions? Witness JF-018, this then concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. You are excused. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we take the break now. We'll have a break for half an hour and we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Usher, could you please hand out the solemn declaration to the witness. And may I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Hoffmann, any matter we should deal with in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, then let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Hoffmann, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. The Court has ordered certain protective measures with respect to you and your evidence here today. These include the use of a pseudonym, face and voice distortion. I will not refer you to by your name but instead by your pseudonym JF-036.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And I would like to ask the Court Usher to bring up the pseudonym sheet which is 65 ter 5277 on the screen, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, Witness, if I can ask you to look at the name that is displayed on this pseudonym sheet and the date of birth, if both are correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And as you can see, a number of persons are listed on this sheet as well as locations that you can refer to by number or letters in public session instead of using the real names, and I would ask the Court Usher to hand out a paper copy of this sheet so you have this at hand if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this pseudonym sheet into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P341 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P341 is admitted under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would then ask that we see 65 ter 5136 on the screen, not to be broadcast again. It's an ICTY witness statement of this witness dated 10 March and 2nd May 2001 and bears the ERN 0303-3589 to 0303-3603.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen before you, you see a document purporting to be a statement that you gave to the ICTY in March and May 2001. Do you recall giving such a statement to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 17 in the English document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise your own signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review this statement in your own language prior to testifying today?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we could briefly look at page 21 in the original and page 18 in the translation. It is chart 3 which is attached to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, this chart refers to the time-period 1993 to 1996. Is it correct that you would like to clarify that this chart refers to that time-period but that you are not sure if all the persons mentioned in this chart had their position as indicated for the full time-period between 1993 and 1996?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, at one point in that period between 1991 and 1996 they were in the position as shown here on this chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. And with that clarification, did your statement that you signed in 2001 accurately reflect what you told the Office of the Prosecutor at the time?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today in court that you were asked in 2001, would you give the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would ask that the prior statement of this witness from 2001 be admitted into evidence under seal, that is, 65 ter 5136.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P342 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P342 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, now that your written statement is admitted into evidence, I'm going to read out a short summary of your written statement for the benefit of the public. This will not be considered as evidence, however, I ask you to carefully listen to the summary. Witness JF-036 gives evidence about operations of the militia, of the so-called SAO SBWS. He describes the influence of the SDS Baranja before the war started in the municipalities and describes a meeting of the commanders of the local Serb Territorial Defence headquarter in Jagodnjak which was attended by leaders of the SDS in Baranja. At this meeting, the TO discussed with which units would participate in an attack on Bilje. The role and organisation of the so-called crisis committees in Baranja is explained. The SDS leadership directed the appointment of the local crisis committees' presidents. The crisis committees also handled the property left behind by refugees who fled the area. Before the JNA took over the territory of Baranja, a number of people that were affiliated with a counter intelligence group KOG of the 2nd JNA Administration obtained weapons and they were arming the Serb population. The weapons they were getting were old fashioned and were stored for a long time. The weapons were brought in civilian trucks, concealed among other goods, and then distributed in Baranja beginning in May 1991 but not to all villages at the same time. In the villages, the SDS members were in charge of the distribution. The witness describes the role and organisation of the state security DB centre of Beli Manastir after October 1991 as well as the chain of command of the police and DB in the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem up to Goran Hadzic. The arrival in the region of representatives of the DB from Sombor in September 1991 is explained. In addition to the local chain of command, the DB centre Beli Manastir had also a chain of command towards the Serbian Ministry of Interior in Belgrade. The DB from Belgrade appointed Radoslav Kostic as a key person in Baranja. Kostic was able to deliver exclusive weapons to important individuals to bribe them, including Heckler Koch, Smith & Wessons, silencers, and similar weapons. Kostic had the final say about what was reported to Belgrade. The witness also gives evidence about the arrest of non-Serb people in Baranja in the second half of 1991. The reasons for the arrests were various, for example, being Croat, being a member of the HDZ, being wealthy, or for revenge. The arrested people would be escorted to Beli Manastir and detained in the prison located in the basement of the militia building. They were often mistreated there. The SUP Beli Manastir organised the transport of the detainees to Dalj and Borovo in order to be exchanged. In all, the witness is aware of some 50 to 80 people who were arrested and transported to Dalj and Borovo, some of whom were later released, but a large number of them disappeared. The witness also gives evidence about the activities of the unit for anti-terrorist operations, JATD, based in Tito's castle in Tikves in the national park of Kopacki Rit. Members of this special unit began operating in Baranja in early 1992. They wore red berets and green camouflage uniforms of a different pattern than the one used by the JNA. They were armed with automatic assault rifles without straps and had belts made of special material and not made of leather. They used Motorola walkie-talkies. They reported to the DB of the Republic of Serbia. Members of this unit were responsible for the abduction of five villagers from Grabovac. And finally the witness states that when the re-integration of the region was inevitable, the DB Belgrade controlled the transport of property from the SAO region towards Serbia. He testifies about how the head of the JATD Vasilije Mijovic who had been sent from Belgrade blackmailed rich people in the region and force local criminals to work for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, I'll continue with a number of questions now. At page 4 of your statement which is now Exhibit P342 in the English version of page 3 in B/C/S of your statement you state that the Territorial Defence TO of your region reported to Zagreb to the Republic of Croatia prior to the war, but after the elections in 1990, the chain of command had to change, you said. Can you explain to the Court which chain of command applied to the TO in the SAO SBWS from 1991 onwards?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: After the conflict broke out between Serbs and Croats, there was a physical breakdown in all communications. Reports were no longer sent, the two opposing enemy sides never reported to each other about any of their plans. To put it simply, Baranja is a territory with a single territorial Defence staff in Beli Manastir had to rely on Serbia because that was there only geographical physical connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did the Serb autonomous region of Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem, the SAO SBWS, have its own organs, institutions, and a government?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: The autonomous province did have its Assembly and organs of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court if within the SAO the laws of Croatia still applied?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... there were no longer applied. The Croatian laws no longer applied there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Further at page 3 of your statement, Exhibit P342, you talk about the Serb Crisis Staff in the region, especially in the villages, and at the end of the relevant paragraph, you state that these Serb Crisis Staff also handled the property that was left behind by refugees. Can you explain how that property of refugees who left was handled in the region?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: One of the tasks of the Crisis Staff was to make a record of all those and to seal all the property that was left behind the refugees by those who fled the villages. This was done by the Crisis Staff of every community or of every village or town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And what happened to that sealed property at any later stage, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Later on, that property was given to refugees who had fled the rest of Croatia and arrived in Baranja. In other words, it was given to other refugees who needed to be accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, from 1991 to 1995, how many official border crossings were there between the Republic of Serbia and the territory of the SAO SBWS?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: The Danube was the natural border. There were just three bridges: Batina, Erdut, and Ilok. And those were the only official crossing points.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for your information, all these places can be found on map 18 in the Court binder which is Exhibit P9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, and that is at pages 11 and 12 in English and page 9 in B/C/S, you have mentioned a number of non-Serbs who were arrested in Baranja and then deported to Slavonia and later went missing. You mentioned, for example, the following persons: Ivan Zelember, Rudolf Jukic, Erne or Ernest Baca, Karlo Rajic, and Simon Mihajlo. Do you have any information about their fate as of today?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, some are still considered missing. And as for the others, it is known that they were killed, they were never exchanged for incarcerated Serbs as had been expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement you state that about 50 to 80 people were arrested and then transported to Slavonia and just for the record in the relevant section in your statement you referred to non-Serbs. Were these 50 to 80 people that were arrested all of non-Serb ethnicity, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record and for your information, some of these persons mentioned are in fact victims of the charged killings in this case. Ivan Zelember is listed as a victim under paragraph 36 of the third amended indictment and Rudolf Jukic, Ernest Baca, Karlo Rajic, and Simon Mihajlo are listed as victims in paragraph 37 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement - that is in English on page 13, B/C/S page 10 and 11 - you describe how a special unit was operating in Baranja in early 1992, a unit that was called JATD. You state that they had a base at Tito's castle in Tikves and the national park called Kopacki Rit. My question to you: Did that special unit go by any specific name or nickname at the time?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: The unit members wore red berets and those red berets gave them the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever have any personal contacts, official or unofficial, with members of that unit in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: I had a few unofficial contacts, they would drop by in our office in the morning to have a cup of coffee or a refreshment, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement further on, on the same reference, you state that the JATD did report to the Serbian state security, the DB. My question to you is: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: They did not communicate with us through official channels. We did not co-operate in terms of intelligence services. They arrived with representatives of the state security of Serbia who introduced some of them to us and we accepted them as a unit that belonged neither to the Baranja TO nor to the JNA, so we accepted them as representatives of the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would like to ask that we see Exhibit P9 on the screen, that is the map 18 from the Court binder, and that shows the area of the SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you have mentioned that the red berets or the JATD had a camp at Tikves in Tito's castle. Would you please, with the Court Usher's help, mark the location on this map with a red cross, please.

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would then ask that you please also put your pseudonym and today's date maybe in the right corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this map Exhibit P9 as marked by this witness into evidence. Again, it's a map of the region of the SAO SBWS, and the witness indicated Tikves on this map, a place where the Red Berets had a camp in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P343, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be admitted - let me see what -- one second. Yes, can be admitted as a public document. Therefore P343 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, that is at page 7 in English, page 6 in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Hoffmann, you earlier dealt with their names listed on page 11, and then the witness said -- I was a bit confused by this list of names, also if you look at the top line of page 12, because - and I'm asking you a specific question, Witness JF-036 - you've say I personally know a number of people who were transported to Dalj and Borovo and later on went missing. Now, you dealt with all those on page 11 apart from one, and then on page 12 at the top a name is mentioned and there you say, I saw him after the war. He survived as he managed to be exchanged. Two years ago he died. Which means that apparently you are listing persons indicate that they went missing although apparently not all of them went missing or temporarily missing because one was exchanged. Now, if you don't say from those you mentioned, that is Baca, Rajic, Simon, Jukic, and Zelember, you said some are still considered missing and others we know died. Could you tell us which one you know have died and which ones you mentioned are still considered to be missing? Let's take them one by one. Baca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure about him. I believe that he has gone missing. That he is still on the missing persons list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Missing up until today? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rajic, Karlo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Simon, Mihajlo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Jukic, Rudolf.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is still missing as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Zelember, Ivan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And why do you believe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you know, I'm not sure. I believe that I have heard from somebody that he was killed. That is a common knowledge. But I'm not a hundred per cent sure that I'm right when I say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So effectively you say all of those mentioned by Mr. Hoffmann are still missing apart from Mr. Zelember where there are indications, although you are not able to further specify, that he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement at page 7 English and page 6 in B/C/S you give evidence about Radoslav Kostic, how he was appointed by the state security DB as a key person for Baranja, and that he reported directly to Belgrade. My question to you: Have you personally seen, either officially or unofficially, Radislav Kostic in 1991 in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe any of those occasions when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: He frequently came over to our offices. He came to see the person under number 1 listed here. He came both officially and unofficially. He would come in whenever he pleased. Sometimes that happened on several days in a row and sometimes he would show up after five to seven days. So it wasn't a regular -- these weren't regular visits. But he did visit frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Have you personally attended any such meetings with Kostic?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about what kind of meetings these were that he did attend?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Among other things, we submitted our reports to the chief who collected them and frequently he would say Kostic is coming over so I would send it forward through him. And then when he came, he described what the situation was like and information that he was actually -- that he received from Kostic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point in time the Prosecution would like to tender two reports compiled by Radoslav Kostic in April 1991 into evidence. This is 65 ter 4298 with ERN 0608-4135 to 0608-4136. That Exhibit is part of the first Bar table motion filed on 25 November 2009, and it was received in response to RFA 1333 from Serbia. Prosecution basically tenders also at this point in time this document from the Bar table because the witness has no direct knowledge of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are doing it at this moment because the context is there. Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar, the two reports.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 4298 becomes Exhibit P344, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the two reports under one 65 ter number P344, two reports are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, and I'm now referring to page 15, you refer to the JATD commanded by Vaso Mijovic and you refer to a time when the reintegration was inevitable. What year did Mijovic come to the area of Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: That was in 1995 sometime mid-year. I couldn't be more precise about the date, so it was in 1995 about middle of the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did that unit, the JATD under Mijovic, go by any name or nickname?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: They also had red caps and we kept calling them still the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you come across any members of the JATD or the Red Berets in 1995 yourself?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Unofficially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And how frequent would that be?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, it was impossible not to run into them because they had check-points. Sometimes they stopped us, sometimes they didn't. In other words, they had the check-point on the road that I had to take and they stopped vehicles. So you couldn't pass on that road without actually seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what the purpose of their presence in 1995 was?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, in my view, there were several reasons for their presence. First of all, after a certain time, they actually conducted mobilisation and trained their men. The second reason was this: After Operation Storm, the Croatian Operation Storm, the civilian population, the people, were very scared; and in order to stop people from leaving Baranja, they did this. So these would be some of the reasons for their presence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Are you aware of any camps the JATD or the Red Berets under Mijovic had in the area of Baranja in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: As far as I know, his staff was in Bilje village in another castle, and the training camps for the training of those mobilised recruits were in the place under A and also at Petrovo Selo which was a place not far from the Hungarian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And just for the record, if you refer to the place under A you are referring to the pseudonym sheet in front of you; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: You have mentioned two training camps. Can you tell the Court who was trained at these two camps?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, at these training camps they trained young men who had turned 18, because during that war there was no regular classic training for young men, and it was the first time on this occasion during the war that somebody actually began training young men for military service in an organised manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement, and it's still page 15 in English, you state that the Belgrade DB organised a transfer of property. Can you explain what you mean by "transfer of property"?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: In the aftermath of Operation Storm it became more or less clear to everyone that Croatia would either by force or by peaceful reintegration recover the territory where we were active, and it was decided that state property, machines, equipment, wheat, corn, grain, and so on, that it be transferred to Serbia. In other words, material goods were being transferred. Because there were these check-points controlled by the Red Berets controlling all the traffic towards the border, they also checked or controlled the export or transfer of these material goods out of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement if you refer to the Belgrade DB, do you refer to the local state security of the city of Belgrade, or do you refer to the Serbian state security?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: I refer to the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you personally meet or see officially or unofficially Vasilije Mijovic in Beli Manastir or elsewhere in Baranja in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes, there were unofficial meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember any specific occasion when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: When the young men who were being trained were being actually matriculated, when there was the celebration where they graduated, Mijovic addressed these young men in a meeting which was attended both by the young trainees and their family members, friends, and so on, so there was a large group of people there, and he addressed the local people, the parents of these young men, and impressed them as a strategic thinker and someone who would take care of these young men, who were to take part in the defence in the remaining Serbian parts on the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Was there, if any, relationship between the JATD and the local police in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no mutual co-operation. Mijovic's unit was independent; it had an agenda of its own. Whereas the local police had their own tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement, and we are still at page 15 in English, you state that Vasilije Mijovic was sent to the region to put the situation under full control of the Belgrade DB. Can you tell the Court how did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, in the context of that statement in view of the fact that Mijovic was the one who conducted the mobilisation and who actually had control of all traffic in and out of Baranja and also because at the time the chief of the DB centre was actually replaced by the Serbian DB, in other words, the entire leadership was actually appointed by the Serbian DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement you also mention a number of names, people you say were criminals and who worked for Mijovic. In that context you often mention stolen cars. Do you have any personal knowledge of any activity with regard to the stolen cars?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not just cars. I think in my statement I mentioned vehicles. In other words, cars, trucks, motor bikes, all-terrain vehicles, so that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And do you have any personal knowledge about the registration process for these stolen cars or stolen vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Most of these vehicles were registered in a very abbreviated procedure, and licences were issued where the owners themselves would fill out forms. In other words, the forms were blank and all you had to do was just fill out the information relating to the vehicle itself and the driver or owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Was Mijovic and his unit involved in that process, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Individuals, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Among the names that you mentioned who worked for Vaso Mijovic is a certain Predrag Radetic. Do you recall if he went by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: His nickname was "Brada."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: "Beard" in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And what was his relation with Mijovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, Mijovic was his witness at his wedding. He was married in Baranja and Mijovic was his witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Is that what you refer to in the Serbian language as "kum"?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes. So he was the witness at his wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with a company called Remont in Beli Manastir? It's spelled R-e-m-o-n-t.

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes. Remont is a large company and one of its activities was repair and maintenance of all kinds of machines and equipment. There was also a workshop which inspected vehicles. In other words, the paperwork for a vehicle would be entered at the workshop there. They would enter the information on the vehicle identification number, colour of the vehicle, type of vehicle, and so on, and all this paperwork would finally end up at the police where the vehicle would be registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was this company Remont in any way involved in the registration process for the stolen cars and vehicles that you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Without Remont, no vehicle would be issued any registration papers by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we see the next Prosecution exhibit, 65 ter 1706 on the screen. It bears ERN 0306-6887 to 0306-6894 in English. It is a report on the abuse of positions by members of the JATD in Baranja and attached are a number of forms that are partly dated September, October, or November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, did you have a chance to review this document prior to your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And judging by your own knowledge, what you just testified now, would you say that the information contained in that document seems to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And Mijovic is listed as a commander of a unit for anti-terrorist operations. Is that consistent with your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: This report mentions a certain Gavric - and that's in English on page 2 and I believe in B/C/S at the end of page 1. A certain Gavric, G-a-v-r-i-c, is mentioned whose car was allegedly taken away by Mijovic and his men. And then this Gavric was finally forced to join the unit. Are you familiar with this person by name Gavric?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: I don't know a person by the name of Gavric. But looking at the description of the event described here, I believe that it should actually be a nickname Gavro. That is not really a name but, rather, the pet name for Zeljko Milovanovic, aka Gavro.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Is that the same Zeljko Milovanovic, aka Gavro, that you mention in your statement at page 15 of the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. Mr. Hoffmann's question -- I have an objection to his question because Mr. -- the witness said that he doesn't know who this Gavric person is and he is just assuming that it could be Gavro. And now my learned colleague is trying to suggest that this was the same person that he mentioned in his statement, and I believe that this is a leading question. The witness was clear, he doesn't know the Gavric, and he is just assuming that it might -- that this might actually refer to a nickname Gavro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, wouldn't it be good to explore the factual basis on which the witness made his assumptions or statements before we ask him whether a person as described Mr. Gavric, which could well be Mr. Gavro, and then I talked about a Mr. Gavro ... so to find the factual basis for what seem to be conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think he did indicate that he looked at what was described in this incident which is why he made that assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, of course, I didn't want to change that, but he did mention a certain Gavro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But even if you look at the incident, then I would like to know what he looked at exactly. If you say, well, this incident looks very much as what I'm familiar with a certain person does. I hear someone shouting and I say, Well, it must be he and he, this person, because I know that he is often shouting. Nevertheless, that might not be conclusive. So we do not even know exactly what the incident the witness referred to as a basis for his assumptions. So if you would explore that, that would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you have mentioned a certain Zeljko Milovanovic, aka Gavro. What do you know about him being involved with the Mijovic unit?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: We have just mentioned the fact that Mijovic tried to put under his control all criminals in Baranja. Zeljko Milovanovic was at the top of that criminal berg, and he was a very capable criminal, and he resisted the longest to Mijovic's attempt. He fled, he hid, Mijovic was looking for him for days in order to woo him over to his side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, proceed, Mr. Hoffmann. Yes, I'm thinking, but it has not led to any conclusion or question yet. Please proceed. If I try to switch off my microphone. I know what happened, the map was on the priority button which -- where it should not be. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this Exhibit 16 -- 1706 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We object to the admission of the exhibit on two grounds. One is authenticity. We don't have any explanation as to the origins of this document, who produced it, who sent it to the -- well, first of all, who sent it to the Prosecution, where it came from, who drafted it, nothing which indicates this is anything other than a forgery. As to relevance, we would submit the following: Firstly, the contents appear to deal with what is a form of criminality which on the face of it isn't related to this indictment. Secondly, in that vein, the witness hasn't been able to properly identify this document or the contents of the document, and the discussion that's just taken place concerning Gavric is a good illustration of that lack of identification. The description of Gavric in this document and the events concerning Gavric are somewhat different, we would submit, to that described at page 15 of the witness's statement. In the witness's statement, P342, Gavric is clearly identified. He is clearly identified by name. He is clearly identified as a local criminal. He is clearly identified as someone who Mijovic was attempting to have work for him in the capacity of a continuation of criminal activity such as the vehicle business described. In this proposed exhibit, Gavric first of all is a different name. Secondly, the description, we would submit, bears little relation to that in the statement, simply the identification of Mijovic beating up a man called Gavric and forcing him to become a member of the JATD unit. Somewhat different, we would submit. Those are our submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann -- Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether I should add something before Mr. Hoffmann can reply to both of our submissions. I agree with what Mr. Jordash has just said, and I subscribe to his words fully. I would like to say that in addition to this document not having a date, a signature, the title explanation looks as if this is an excerpt from an entirely different document. Therefore, I totally agree with my learned friend and I object to the admission of this document into evidence and especially to the admission of the document though this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your colleague doesn't say that it's an excerpt from another document but that it's a forgery, but -- or at least that there's nothing to believe that it's anything else than a forgery, which is short, it's a short -- he said it's likely a forgery. Mr. Hoffmann, could you shed some light, first of all, on the provenance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. This document has actually been provided by Zoran Lilic who's former president of the Republic of Yugoslavia. It was provided to the OTP when he was interviewed for the Milosevic case in which he testified publicly. And this document was provided in December 2001 to the Office of the Prosecutor. Insofar as to the origin of this document, of course there is no dispute about it that this particular document, those two pages, have no official letterhead or stamp or signature. I do invite the Chamber to look at the following pages from page 3 onwards where we do see a number of official forms that are attached to this document. And in terms of the arguments about the contents of this document, I submit that it's -- the large majority of this document completely in line with what the witness testified today. It does talk about the JATD being active in Baranja. It does talk about Mijovic being commander. It does mention Mijovic's men nicknamed Brada, the same person that the witness mentioned today. The document talks about the smuggling and re-sale of stolen cars through Mijovic and his men, again absolutely what the witness testified to today. And finally it does mention the registration process and the involvement of the Remont company, again something the witness just testified to. And those attachments are actually attachments from the Remont company and relate to individual vehicles. And I think at least on one of them, I think it's on page 3 of the document, even the name Mijovic is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could my learned friend Mr. Hoffmann tell us whether this document was received from Mr. Lilic as a separate document, just two pages, or whether it was part of a bigger document or part of another document? If it was received as a part of a different document, then we would very much like to see the entire document. What I'm after is to find out whether only these two pages have been handed over by Mr. Lilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: May I just respond on this very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, unless you want to add something to this question, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: As regards Mr. Lilic, I could add one thing which is - and so far from the Defence perspective we don't take a position on this - but I would, for point of information, submit to the Trial Chamber that Mr. Lilic was put forward in the Milosevic case as a witness who could not -- who the Prosecution did not necessarily rely upon completely for the truth of what he was saying - let me put that differently - that they couldn't necessarily put him forward as a witness of truth. That's the way he was put forward by Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then apparently in some respects --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In some respects he could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise you could call him as a witness if -- so Mr. Nice apparently then was not convinced that every respect he would speak the truth. Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I cannot talk on behalf of Mr. Geoffrey Nice and what was said at the time. All I have at my hand is currently the information that this document was provided as such by Mr. Zoran Lilic including the attachments which are also part of this Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not as part of a bigger document. I think the Chamber needs some time to -- because the issue apparently is whether this is a truthful forgery, isn't it, that the testimony is that these were all false documents to be filled in by persons themselves, so therefore, not the real documents. That's at least what I understood from the witness, that through the Remont company that you would just produce some paperwork. So what we are actually looking at at this moment is whether these are the real forgeries or that they are not. Is that more or less ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In a way, yes, they were forgeries then, but of course as such they would be authentic exhibits in this case. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, no, I see these are authentic, in your view, authentic examples of forged documents. Okay. We'll have -- perhaps we have to look at -- there's -- of course there's another matter remaining, Mr. Hoffmann. You asked the witness, Is that the same Zeljko Milovanovic also known as Gavro that you mentioned in your statement, page 15 of the original. Could you tell me where on page 15 the witness mentions Zeljko Milovanovic also known as Gavro?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I have to correct that, in fact, it does say only Gavro Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so what you introduce in your question is that Gavro is a nickname which is then, by the way, that's not supported in any way by the statement. Second, that Gavro is the same as Gavric. And then I asked you to explore the factual basis on which such conclusions were made. And, well, you moved rather quickly to tendering the document rather than to positively responding to my invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If I may just add on that, I think actually whether or not this Gavric is the same person that the witness described as Zeljko Milovanovic, aka Gavro, I think is, for the admission of this document, certainly of minor importance because it's one of the examples how Mijovic unit operated in Baranja. He clearly stated, and there is no dispute about that, that he doesn't know a name by Gavric, he only then said this may well be Zeljko Milovanovic Gavro. And only on that second name that he mentioned, I wanted to clarify if that is the same person that he mentions or if there are two Zeljko Milovanovic, aka Gavro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
