utterances.text: Yes, so you say that the core of the relevance is not the identity, the Gavro/Gavric issue but it's, rather, the functioning of the - what was the name of that company again? - Remont company irrespective of -- and that's what the witness testified about. So then the authenticity of the document remains. Any further comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I would reiterate our objection concerning relevance to the indictment. This is 1995. This is criminality which is a long way away from what the indictment alleges. And we would submit that simply adducing evidence of criminality by those who during the indictment period are said to have been members of the DB isn't a sufficient indication of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honours, A, the indictment does cover the period from 1991 to 1995 in terms of persecution, deportation, forcible transfer. It does to a large extent concern these special units of the Serbian state security otherwise known as Red Berets or the JATD. We have here a member, a high ranking member, of as we say, Mijovic. If there would be no dispute in this trial about Vasilije Mijovic being a member of the Serbian state security being sent to the region on behalf of the Serbian state security, we could probably do without this document, but at this point in time we have to prove every single puzzle in this piece, and that is part of it. Plus, the relevance, I think, also stems from that this evident, this document, clearly corroborates what the witness has testified which just adds to the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, you say it's the link of Mijovic to the Serbian state security rather than that he may have misbehaved, that he was not an angel in his private life as a -- in commerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if I may add, the person of Vasilije Mijovic will pop up at different parts of this trial in different crime basis and especially he does play a crucial role when it comes to the events in July 1995 in Trnovo where a number of documents and witnesses will talk about his role. And even more so we have to prove that link between the person Mijovic and the two accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mijovic being linked or being a member of the Serbian the state security?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If my learned friends are suggesting that this type of criminality which, as I understand the Prosecution submissions on this, concerns criminality against Serbians, if that is not to be relied upon by the Prosecution in support of the indictment but what they are seeking to do is to link Mijovic to the accused, then we withdraw the objection on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what is your view on that matter? Apparently we are trying to focus on what the possible probative value is. And I do understand that stealing a car doesn't mean stealing a car from someone from another ethnicity. So if that's taken out as a relevant matter and you said the core of your problem was to link Mr. Mijovic to the Serbian state security, then it seems that we are close to not too much disagreement. But, Mr. Bakrac, now, you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with Mr. Jordash has just said. If you look at the statement a little bit better, you will see that the witness also mentions cars that had arrived from western Europe, so they had nothing whatsoever to do with the cars that had been seised by members of another ethnic group. And at the end of the day you will see that we have already offered some pieces of evidence, and you will see that during our cross-examination, showing that different property and vehicles had been taken away from criminals and the record was kept of that. This document certainly has to be marked for identification, but we do not agree that this document should be admitted into evidence. When you look at the evidence offered by the Defence, I believe that we can re-open the issue of this document and discuss it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what the Chamber understands is that where the cars were stolen and from whom is not the vital probative element in this document. Secondly, it seems, but correct me when I'm wrong, that the Defence is relatively relaxed if it comes to establishing a link between Mijovic and the Serbian state security because then they even give up their objection against the documents which would be a forgery, so that's very generous, or at least there's nothing which indicates that it's not a forgery. But at least there seems to be not a major dispute about what you are seeking to establish primarily through this document and what the Defence is, well, willing to accept. I do not know exactly what you are accepting, so therefore you are invited to see whether you can come to an agreement on those matters. And then, Mr. Hoffmann, then we can do two things. If you come to an agreement, you could either for the time being withdraw the document, or leave it as marked for identification, which means that for the month to come we have now and then to have a look at it again and to see whether we have resolved matters on such as authenticity. And may I invite the parties to see what is possible in this respect and then at this moment no decision yet is taken, not even on the status of this document, before you have met with the Defence. And the other matters while you said the person is not Gavric, Gavro, that seems not to be really an important matter. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, I may have misunderstood you. I am trying to listen the interpretation and to look at the transcript at the same time. I did not understand that Mr. Jordash said that this document could establish a link and that we would agree to this document establishing a link between Vasiljevic and the DBR of the Republic of Serbia. If that's the way you understood it and if that's the way Mr. Jordash said, then our position is different. We don't think that a link can be established between the DBR Serbia and Vasilije Mijovic by means of this document. Our position is not the same. It's contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clarify. I did say that we withdraw the objection on that particular point. We stick by the objection to authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now matters really become complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, to interrupt. My client would like to use the restroom if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are at the time where we would have a break anyhow. So let's think about and most likely the outcome will be - but I have to discuss it with my colleagues - to have the document MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for Your Honours' information, I would make one more comment before the break. And I've indicated that to both Defence teams I would like, at a later stage, to actually tender basically from the Bar table a few excerpts from the personnel files from the state security of Serbia which goes to the same matter. I've raised that earlier with the Defence. I have no clear indication yet as to whether there are any objections, but it's in the same context of Mijovic and the Serbian state security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have a break first. We'll have a break and resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Very quickly, Your Honours, I have briefly discussed with the Defence again during the break. There is no change in position so to say. There are still objections to the document admission. While on our side we would ask that this document be tendered into evidence, I think we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to ask us whether it be tendered, that's for you to do, and then we'll decide on whether it will be admitted or not. You still tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Point taken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be assigned a number. It will be marked for identification. The Chamber will first have a closer look at it and then see whether it can decide -- whether it can decide at this moment about admission, whether or not after having asked for further submissions by the parties. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P345, marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would then ask that we see the next exhibit on the screen, that is, 65 ter 4809. It's a newspaper article from 31st July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: It is a newspaper article from the magazine or newspaper "Nasa Borba" and the headline reads "when liberators loot." And the Prosecution received this article actually in response to an RFA 1333 from the Republic of Serbia in March 2007. It was preselected by members of the OTP when screening some of the archives provided by the Serbian DB earlier on and then was submitted by Serbia with that response. Sir, you have testified about the issue of stolen cars and the involvement of Mijovic's unit in this process in 1995 in Baranja. Did you have a chance to review this article prior to testifying today?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you also look at the report about the Salajic family which is in B/C/S starting on the second page and in English in the second paragraph on the first page. Are you familiar with the Salajic family?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Yes, I know the family Salajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And have you heard anything about how this family was approached and their cars were taken away?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, I heard about that incident. This is an old family, well off, from Jagodnjak village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And in the part about the Salajic family, it does read that someone mentions that the unit was allegedly stationed at Bilje. Do you know of any unit that was stationed at that time in Bilje?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: At the time, the only unit, the command unit, was the Vaso Mijovic unit at the time stationed in Bilje. We already mentioned earlier that they were at an old castle in Bilje.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we can please go to page 4 of the English translation and back to page 1 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: There is a text box in the original on page 1 headed "Who is Colonel Mijovic." And it does read in the article, and I quote: "When Vasilije Mijovic came to Baranja, he freely introduced himself as Colonel of the UDBA," that is the state security administration, "sent personally by Slobodan Milosevic and Jovica Stanisic, chief of the Serbian state security, to establish order." Sir, is that information consistent with your own knowledge and experience in Baranja in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mijovic had that kind of attitude. He saw himself as an authority, and he liked to be in the limelight. And I think that he wasn't described quite truthfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders this article from the 31st July, 1995, 65 ter 4809, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We don't object as such, although could I kindly request that we have a clarification of the last answer, please, before ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jordash, the same thing came into my mind. You said that he wasn't described quite truthfully. Could you tell us in what respect you consider the description of Mr. Mijovic not being truthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say that it was not truthful; I actually said that it was fairly described. I agree with the description given here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And same for the Simatovic Defence? In the absence of any objections, is it to establish that this was said about Mr. Mijovic or do you consider it also an element or at least a probative value as to the truth of its content?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Well, it's, of course, in the first place, a newspaper article from the time that just reports as such. It does corroborate what the witness says, and it does refer to what allegedly Mr. Mijovic himself said when he appeared in Baranja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the absence of any objections, Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 4809 becomes Exhibit P346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P346 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And just for the transcript, it was 65 ter 4809.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, in the same context in your statement at page 7 you also refer to members of the Serbian state security from Sombor which is in Vojvodina in Serbia coming to Baranja in 1991, and you do mention a number of names in your statement. I would ask you now look at a number of lists of persons and see if you recognise any of the names on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And I would ask that we see first 65 ter 5004.1. It is a redacted version of that exhibit to be shown on the screen. It is a payment record seised from the Serbian state security for the JATD in October 1995, and according to the requested protective measures of Serbia we are using the redacted version in public. This exhibit as well as the two following ones are also part of the first Bar table motion of the Prosecution of 25 November 2009. And I will ask that we go to page 46 in both languages first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please zoom in a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If you just carefully review the names starting with number 1 down to the end of the list and tell us if you know any of these persons by number and name.

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Under number 1, Vasilije Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just indicate when you are done with that list we can go to the next page which is actually in reverse order so it would be page 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first hear from the witness. You invited him to say when he was done and then we immediately moved to the next page. So let's go back to the first page. We just move back to the first page, the page we saw before, with number -- Mijovic under number 1. One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under number 1 and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we enlarge a bit. Could you take your time and tell us whether apart from Mr. Mijovic whether you recognise any other name on that list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more names on the first page, the one that's on the monitors now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we now move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't see any names I know here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And finally, if we can then go to page 44 of this exhibit in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under 81, Radmila Spanovic. 88, both the first and last names are familiar, Jovan Opacic. I knew a person by that name who was from Beli Manastir. Number 92, Predrag Radetic. 110, Jovica Zivanov. 111, Jovo Ralic. 112, Dusko Salajic. 116, Zeljko Milovanovic. 119, Damir Matausek and no one else on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, can you tell us who was Radmila Spanovic, number 81 on this list?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Radmila Spanovic worked for a while for the state security at a Beli Manastir centre. She worked there as a secretary. Before that, she worked for the police and then she was transferred to the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Number 111, Jovo Ralic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Jovo Ralic are the -- that's the first and last name of an operative from the Sombor state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And we had some discussion before the break about Zeljko Milovanovic. Did that person go by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Well, that is Gavro.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And the last person you mentioned, Damir Matausek, number 119. Did he also go by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: His nickname was Hipi. "Hipik" in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would then ask that we see the next of such lists, 65 ter 5007.1 on the screen. It is a similar document from the Serbian state security. Now for the second half of October 1995 for the JATD. And I'll ask that we look at first page 45 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We again remind the parties to switch off the microphones once the witness speaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Page 45, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, the same question, if you please carefully review that list before we turn to the next page and if you can identify any name and number on this list?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Number 3, Vasilije Mijovic. Predrag Radetic under 16. And nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to the next page, page 46 of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 53, Jovan Opacic. 56, Radmila Spanovic. 59, Jovica Zivanov, and Jovo Ralic under 60. 65, Zeljko Milovanovic. 68, Damir Matausek. And nobody else on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And finally on this document if we can please go to page 27.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21, Milan Tosic. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Milan Tosic was?

utterances.speaker: JF-036
utterances.text: Milan Tosic was deputy chief of the state security centre in Sombor for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And finally, I would ask that we go to 65 ter 5006.1 at page 60.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21, Milan Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that all these three DB per diem payment records be admitted into evidence. The redacted versions are 65 ter 5004.1, 5006.1, and 5007.1. The unredacted versions have the respected 65 ter numbers without that suffix. And those should be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are seeking admission of the unredacted versions because I think it was this Chamber was not very fond of having two versions of the same document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We certainly leave that in the discretion of the Chamber, in the case of the previous witness JF-005 I think the Chamber actually did admit two versions, one public, one under seal. I think Your Honours were reminded the last time when we had that issue by your own staff that there is actually a decision which stated it should be done that way because that question was also raised last time and then you were, I think, referred to the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I must have -- two weeks out of court is apparently not a good thing for a presiding judge. I hope it was for the others. We'll have numbers assigned. But first, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There is an objection on the basis of relevance. Whilst we understand the relevance of Mijovic appearing on a list which purports to be a list of JATD members, what we haven't been provided with is an indication of the significance of most of the names. Maybe it's a simple inquiry to make of the Prosecution. Do they say that every person on this list was within the JATD unit in Baranja? Do they say this list applied across the board, across the Croatia and Bosnia? It's really a matter of trying to seek some clarification as to the significance of this list. And particularly the names which the witness has identified. If I can just pick out one, the name of Radmila Spanovic, the secretary, appears in this list. The Prosecution case is that the JATD was some kind of special militarised unit, and if we take that witness's evidence at face value, then now this specialised unit has a secretary. And so it's really just trying to seek some clarification as to the exact relevance of these lists to the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree with my learned friend, and I would like to say this: Obviously the witness has told us that, for example, Jovo Ralic was an operative in the Sombor state security. Obviously the list contains the names of many people who had nothing to do with the anti-terrorist unit. Second of all, this is not a payroll. This is a list of daily allowances that could have been paid on any basis. So we challenge the relevance. As I've been looking at maybe 200 pages of these lists, I notice that each list should be finished with a signature and a stamp. There is one such list, but it seems that every list is a list -- a separate list. Maybe my learned friend Hoffmann can help me. So, for example, the list doesn't start with 23 as it should, after number 22 on the previous list, but it starts with number 1. So we don't know what lists apply to who these people are and in what respect were the daily allowances paid. And I don't think that this witness is able to tell us all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware that of course, in relation to this list, there may be a lot of questions remaining, but at this moment it cannot be said that these lists do not meet the requirements of relevance. Not to say that every item and every entry on the list that the relevance is already clear, but it cannot be said that these lists lack relevant or probative value and still to be seen what exactly can be proven by those lists or not. But, therefore, the Chamber denies the objections. Madam Registrar, the numbers to be assigned would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 5004 becomes Exhibit P347. 65 ter 5006 becomes Exhibit P348. 65 ter 5007 becomes Exhibit P349, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P347 up to and including P349 are admitted into evidence. And then the redacted versions I'll have a closer look at what the Chamber decided earlier, but, of course, that is a matter of administrative -- yes, it's a matter of administration and has no substance. So, therefore, that will be -- we'll look at that and act accordingly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, those should be admitted under seal because those are the unredacted ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the unredacted ones. And these are the unredacted ones admitted under seal, P347, P348, and P349.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As I indicated prior to the break, the Prosecution would like to tender a few parts of the DB personnel file for Vasilije Mijovic. Basically in the context of this witness testimony about Mijovic but from the Bar table and with no further questions to be put to this witness. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defences aware of what these documents are?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, they have been included in the respective notification for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Usually if we have, well, I think, the context is clear here so that we would not urge you at this moment to create a kind of a table. It is all about documents from the personnel file of Mr. Mijovic. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not altogether sure which ones the Prosecution are now indicating. I think -- I don't think there's going to be much dispute, but I would like to be sure which ones are included, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly. Those are currently five excerpts. Those are Exhibit 65 ter 4469, it is a receipt signed by Mr. Mijovic that he received a red beret and a badge for the red beret. It is then 65 ter 4930, a document that in fact relates to the Kula camp video, Exhibit P61. We then have 65 ter 4932, a certificate that Mijovic was a member of the JATD of the Serbian state security signed by Milan Radonjic. Then 65 ter 5164, document dated from 1997, a request by the accused Franko Simatovic from a local police station to return a weapon that was seised from Mr. Mijovic. And finally 65 ter 5165. This is a document that includes personal details of the candidate being Mijovic where it is stated that he served in the unit since 1991. Now, I want to add, actually, one matter on this exhibit. These are currently only excerpts from the file. We have been notified by the Simatovic Defence of a number of exhibits they may want to use during their cross-examination. In light of some of those documents, as well, maybe in the interest of the Chamber, we could also offer to tender the whole personnel file as one exhibit, if that would be preferred. I think it's a total number of about 40 pages. All have been translated and disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not having seen it, the Chamber has no clear preference. I mean, it depends what the other documents tell us. So, therefore, if we will come close to the whole of the 40 pages by all those documents to be tendered by the Defence, then it makes sense to have it in its entirety. But otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Your Honours, I didn't indicate that the Defence is actually tendering parts of it, but they tendered some other documents and it may be then for us to tender other parts to put the Defence documents into context, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but this Chamber is not very much in favour of having more in evidence that is -- but we would have to decide on the relevance of all those other documents. Not even knowing what they are, I think this is to be preferred. Any objections against the five documents, the five excerpts mentioned by Mr. Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think only an objection insofar as the description of Exhibit 5164 which my learned friend just described, I think, as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the description is not evidence. It's on the record. And if you carefully look at how it is introduced in e-court, and the description, and to try to agree with Mr. Hoffmann what would be the right description, it not being evidence, the evidence is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then, Madam Registrar, let me just refer to the 65 -- Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I apologise, I may have not reacted well in time, however when it comes to 65 ter document 4469, I challenge the authenticity of this document. It is not clear who handed it over. Maybe we should have it on the screen. There is a stamp in the left corner of the Republic of Serbia, but it -- the document was never recorded in the files. And there is just one signature without a stamp standing for the person who handed it over. We challenge the authenticity of the 65 ter document 4469. As far as document 4932, document on 65 ter list is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment. Could we have 65 ter 4469 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the left-hand side corner, you will see a stamp of the Ministry of the Interior, but there's no number for the file. There is no date when the document was filed. And when it says "handed over" or "received by," there is a signature but the stamp is missing, although it was customary. In the right-hand side, there is a file number and a date, but it is not clear where these originate from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else on the authenticity?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This could have been typed up by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, for the sake of comparison, if we look at the following document that the Defence doesn't challenge, it is 65 ter 4932, you will see that there is a number, a date, and Milan Radonjic's signature, and a stamp --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if you do not ask it to be shown on the screen, I do not see anything at all. So if you would please ask for the documents to be shown on the screen so that we are able to do what you suggest we should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, the second document that was tendered by the Prosecution, and I don't challenge that document at all, in the left-hand-side corner you will see the same stamp by the Ministry of the Interior containing a number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what I expect you to do -- the second document to be shown on the screen. So could we have 65 ter 4932 on the screen. Then we can at least look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have it on my screen so it is there unless I've given you the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's -- I see it now as well. So you would say the stamp in the first document is without any numbers and dates filled in in the stamp, and here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And here everything is by the book. According to regulations there is a stamp and there is a stamp and the signature of the person who issued the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as 65 ter 5164 document is concerned, it is -- it was issued in 1997 and signed by Franko Simatovic. So we do not challenge the authenticity of this document. However, the Defence does challenge the relevance of the document. The document was issued in 1997 which is beyond the scope of the indictment, and it says here that a rifle was seised which was property of the state security sector. It doesn't say here how Mr. Mijovic got by it. It doesn't say that Mr. Mijovic was a member of the state security sector. The only thing that is mentioned in here is that the rifle in question is indeed property of the state security sector and this is the crux of our objections and that's why we challenge the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it was received by Mr. Mijovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Obviously there is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we need to have a look at it because that's the way in which --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- because that's how it was described by Mr. Hoffmann. Could we have 5164, 65 ter 5164 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now we have it on the screen. And if you look at the heading, you will see that this was issued by the Ministry of the Interior, the second administration. There is a date. We don't challenge the authenticity, but we do challenge the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we haven't -- at least, I have no English translation yet. Yes. Any further objections, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objections are denied in relation to 65 ter 4469 where the authenticity is challenged. The Chamber sees at this moment in relation to that document no reason to order further evidence of its authenticity. This is not to say that a lack of authenticity cannot be argued by the parties, but at this moment the Chamber does not see on the basis of the submissions made any reason to order further investigations into the authenticity of the document. All the other documents, the issues raised, are more to the weight to be given to that evidence than to admissibility. Madam Registrar, I'll go through the numbers one by one. 65 ter 4469 would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be P350, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. The next one: 65 ter 4930.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P351, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P351 is admitted into evidence. 65 ter 4932.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P352, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P352 is admitted into evidence. 65 ter 5164.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P353, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P353 is admitted into evidence. 65 ter 5165.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P354, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P354 is admitted into evidence. I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Hoffmann, the indication was that you would need two hours, we have now spent two sessions. Where are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am aware of the time. There is one exhibit that is left, it's a video; and I would ask the permission to -- at the beginning of the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would that take?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: There are three clips of total 12 minutes with a very few questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that would take close to 20 minutes. How much time would the Stanisic Defence team need for cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think somewhere between an hour and a half and two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a little bit over one session. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we will need about the same time. But I hope that Mr. Jordash and I will manage to agree not to overlap, and I hope that we will be able to finished with this witness tomorrow. But from where I am at the moment, I believe that I will need anything between an hour and a half to two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For tomorrow, Mr. Hoffmann, 20 minutes for you. Then what remains is if Mr. Jordash and Mr. Bakrac would sit together and see to what extent they could stream-line, then I would say, to start with, each of you the time of a little bit over one session, that's 80 minutes approximately, 75 minutes is a full session. 80 minutes approximately. Then we have two hours and 40 minutes, three hours. And if there are any Chamber questions. That's guidance for the parties for tomorrow. Of course, you never know in advance how matters develop. Witness 36, we would like to see you back tomorrow in the afternoon, and instruct you that you should meanwhile not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony that you've given already today or whether that's testimony still to be given tomorrow. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would like to see you back tomorrow, Tuesday the 13th of April, quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom II.
